correctness.rationale: The order-eight argument is reconstructed from the normalized character matrix: pairwise row orthogonality forces the Fano-plane incidence structure, hence row multiplication closure. Passing to the annihilator quotient gives an eight-element subspace, and a linear complement supplies unique translational factorization. The cardinality-divisibility and four-point cases are proved separately. A standalone checker verifies every labeled Fano system satisfying the row constraints and independently builds a rank-ten order-twelve Paley witness.

originality.rationale: The closest 2019 sources prove the binary cases through dimension six and explicitly use exhaustive computation for size-eight sets in dimensions five and six. Aten et al. only force graph structure at cardinalities \(p\) and \(p^{d-1}\), which does not cover fixed cardinality eight in arbitrary dimension. Exact-form and implication searches found no source asserting the dimension-free subspace-complement theorem or the resulting exact minimum cardinality twelve.
residual_risks: A short unpublished or non-indexed note may already observe the dimension-free eight-point consequence.
The theorem combines classical order-eight Hadamard structure with finite-field spectral machinery, so an equivalent argument could be hidden under different terminology.
Search non-coverage is not treated as proof of absolute novelty.
